title: Micro-SLO adoption playbook — model-serving pilot
content:
Purpose
This note is a working playbook for a 45-day pilot to experiment with ‘micro-SLOs’ for model-serving paths where end-to-end latency/cost/quality tradeoffs can be tuned per feature. The outcome we want: a repeatable cross-functional process (roles, cadence, signals, tooling) for incremental SLO adoption that is low-friction for product teams yet enforces safety and reliability guardrails.

Context / Why micro-SLOs?
- Full-service SLOs are heavy: long discovery, hard to measure for noisy model outputs, and slow to roll out.
- Several model-serving features (embed API, short-chat, reranking) have different risk profiles and cost-sensitivity.
- We hypothesize that adopting small, scoped SLOs for critical call paths will reduce operational overhead and let teams iterate faster.

Scope for pilot
- Target services: hosted embeddings endpoint (route: /v1/embeddings), short-chat route (max tokens <= 128), and reranking pipeline used by Search UX.
- Pilot duration: 45 days (kickoff -> run -> retro).
- Pilot teams: platform-serving, embeddings-product, search-ux, eng-sre, reliability-analytics.

Success metrics (how we’ll judge):
- Process metrics: time from request -> agreed SLO (target < 10 business days), time to instrument metrics (target < 5 days).
- Operational metrics: percent of requests covered by a micro-SLO in pilot routes (target 90%), reduction in P99 latency variance for those routes (target 15% improvement).
- Behavioral metrics: number of rollbacks or emergency overrides triggered (target 0–1).

Definitions (working)
- Micro-SLO: a narrowly scoped SLO (e.g., "Embeddings: prefix-cache-hit P95 < 120ms for requests <=128 tokens") that is easy to measure and maps directly to a single route or small set of routes.
- Owner: team/person accountable for the micro-SLO.
- Steward: SRE contact who helps with instrumenting and runbook.

Pilot playbook (step-by-step)
1) Kickoff (Day 0–2)
  - Identify route owners and SRE stewards. (Action: owners list due EOD Day 0)
  - Quick discovery call (30 min): agree targeted user journeys and what to measure.
  - Output: signed one-pager per route with suggested micro-SLO statement.

2) Instrumentation & dashboarding (Day 3–12)
  - SRE adds minimal metrics and tags (route, model_version, token_count_bucket).
  - Create lightweight dashboard widgets: latency histogram, error types, cost per request estimate.
  - Add a micro-SLO card to Console (experimental panel) with rolling window and burn rate.
  - Deliverable: dashboard link + instrumentation PR.

3) Canary & guardrails (Day 13–25)
  - Implement canary policy for changes affecting the route. Include automated abort if micro-SLO burn rate > 2x baseline.
  - Add a quick rollback play in the runbook for the route.
  - Start 7-day trial traffic shaping for each route (5k small requests min) to gather baseline.

4) Run experiment (Day 26–45)
  - Monitor micro-SLOs daily; SRE/owner check-in bi-weekly.
  - If quality regressions observed, open an evaluation (link to eval harness) and freeze rollout.
  - Record interventions and time-to-detect.

5) Retro & decision (Day 46)
  - Retro with stakeholders: decide whether to scale, iterate, or abandon.
  - Produce a one-page rollout cadence and recommended default templates for future micro-SLOs.

Roles & responsibilities (working)
- Route Owner (product/feature team): propose SLO statement, accept risk, implement product-side changes. 
- SRE Steward (eng-sre): instrument metrics, set alerts, implement canary abort.
- Reliability Analyst (reliability-analytics): baseline measurement, estimate cost impact.
- Platform (serving-runtime): ensure model variants and KV caching metrics are exposed.
- Solutions Eng / CS (if customer-facing): validate customer-impact assumptions.

Example micro-SLO templates (pick one per route)
- Embeddings (small request path): "P95 latency < 150ms for token_count <= 64, measured at edge-inbound route, 14-day rolling window"
- Short-chat (interactive): "P99 first-token latency < 600ms for chat sessions under 128 tokens, 7-day rolling window"
- Reranker: "Error rate (non-200 responses) < 0.5% over 7 days and 99th percentile latency for scoring < 200ms"

Signals to watch (leading & lagging)
- Leading: cache hit ratio changes, model-quantization fallbacks, increase in token_count_bucket > threshold, sudden drop in prefix-KV hit rates.
- Lagging: P95/P99 latency, error rate spikes, customer error reports (CS tickets), rollback events.

Instrumentation checklist
- [ ] Route-level timing (end-to-end)
- [ ] Model decode time and kernel execution time
- [ ] Token count bucket tag
- [ ] Cache hit / miss metric
- [ ] Request attribution (team, feature flag, customer tier)
- [ ] Cost estimate per 1000 requests (daily rollup)

Runbook excerpt (for Embeddings small-path)
- Trigger: micro-SLO burn rate > 1.5x baseline for 30m
- Initial actions:   1) Notify #sre-embeddings and route-owner
                    2) Check recent deploys (gitops history)
                    3) Toggle experimental cache warmers off
                    4) If burn rate persists > 60m, activate rollback and tip scale to lower-capacity variant
- Postmortem: owner to file short postmortem within 72h if rollback occurred

Risk & mitigation notes
- Risk: Too many micro-SLOs become noise. Mitigation: limit to 1–3 per service during pilot, enforce expiry after 6 months unless promoted to full SLO.
- Risk: Measurement mismatches (client vs server clocks, sampling). Mitigation: standardize tracing headers and use server-side timing as canonical.
- Risk: Teams see micro-SLOs as a checkbox. Mitigation: require explicit acceptance of tradeoffs in the one-pager.

Operational tooling asks (engineering backlog items)
- Quick Console card for micro-SLOs (small UI prototype) — PR# open: PR#4523
- Tag-based SLO grouping in Alerts system (epic: ENG-7982)
- Lightweight SLO template generator (CLI) to populate dashboards and runbook snippets

Communication plan
- Week 0: announcement to platform and product mailing lists; invite for kickoff
- During: weekly digest for pilot group (short bulleted summary)
- Post: publish pilot results + template on Confluence and present in Reliability Guild meeting

Meeting cadence (recommended)
- Kickoff: 30 min
- Instrumentation sync: 30 min weekly until dashboards ready
- SRE/Owner standup: bi-weekly 30 min during run window
- Retro: 60 min at the end

Open questions / decisions required
- How do we mark a micro-SLO as permanent vs timeboxed? (proposal: timebox 6 months -> promote)
- What burn-rate threshold should trigger automated aborts for customer-visible routes? (proposal: 2x for 30 min)
- Which telemetry retention tier for micro-SLO dashboards? (proposal: 90 days for pilot)

Next immediate actions (this doc owner)
- Send invites for kickoff (target 2026-03-04)
- Create instrumentation checklist ticket ENG-8124 and assign to SRE steward
- Draft one-pagers for the three pilot routes and circulate for sign-off by 2026-03-06

Notes to self
- Keep language simple in one-pagers; product teams resist heavy SLA templates.
- Prioritize quick wins: dashboards and one clear runbook step are more valuable than 20 metrics.

Appendix: quick links
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RLY/Micro-SLO+Design+Notes
- Jira epic: ENG-7982 (micro-slo tooling)
- Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness

(End of working playbook — leave comments inline; this will be iterated in the pilot)"
